draft.title: Cambodia and the Khmer Rouge
card: The Khmer Rouge was a Cambodian communist movement led by Pol Pot. It captured the capital, Phnom Penh, in April 1975 and ruled Cambodia until 1979.
The regime tried to build a rural, classless society at once. It emptied the cities and forced people to work in the countryside, mostly on farms.
It targeted people it saw as enemies, such as officials, teachers and ethnic minorities. Many died from execution, forced labour, starvation and disease.
About 1.5 to 2 million Cambodians died. The regime ended in 1979 when Vietnam invaded and drove the Khmer Rouge from power.
draft.remember: The Khmer Rouge ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979, and its policies killed about 1.5 to 2 million people.

a.q: What did the Khmer Rouge do soon after capturing Phnom Penh in 1975?
opts: Forced city people to move to the countryside to work
Invited city people to stay and run new factories
Handed power to a government elected by the people
Moved the capital to Hanoi to join North Vietnam
a.why: The regime wanted a rural, classless society, so it emptied the cities and forced people into farm work. It did not build up the cities or seek elections.
a.clue: Think about where the regime wanted people to live and work.

b.q: Which statement best explains how the Khmer Rouge regime in Cambodia ended?
opts: Vietnam invaded in 1979 and drove it from power
The United States invaded in 1975 and removed it
Its own people voted it out at an election in 1977
Pol Pot agreed to hand over power to the Vietnamese
b.why: Vietnam invaded in 1979 and removed the Khmer Rouge from power. The United States was not involved in ending it, and the regime did not fall through an election.
b.clue: The brief names the country whose 1979 invasion ended the regime.

a.best: Forced city people to move to the countryside to work

b.best: Vietnam invaded in 1979 and drove it from power

problems.detail: The clue gives the answer away. It says the regime was ended by a country's '1979 invasion', and only one option mentions both 1979 and an invasion. It also calls the card 'the brief'.

Minor imprecision: Vietnam launched its invasion on 25 December 1978 and took Phnom Penh on 7 January 1979. 'Ended in 1979 when Vietnam invaded' is acceptable as a simplification, but 'Vietnam's invasion, launched in December 1978, drove the Khmer Rouge from Phnom Penh in January 1979' would be more accurate for HSC students.

check.summary: The facts and answers are sound. The clue for question b gives the answer away by naming the 1979 invasion, and the card slightly simplifies the timing of the Vietnamese invasion, which began in December 1978.
